bull_case: 765kV, ESS and power-conversion adjacencies can reshape grid architecture as load complexity rises.
bear_case: Core transformer/switchgear growth is mostly sustaining infrastructure, not 10x disruption.
thesis: HDHE is an innovation beneficiary and capable systems supplier, but its core business is not a classic disruptive-innovation model.

evidence.claim: The company has >1.6GWh cumulative ESS experience and 200MWh Texas / 600MWh Anjwa projects.
2026 includes 765kV UHV transformer orders and U.S. capacity expansion.

counterevidence: Large transformers remain engineered capital goods.
No company-specific 10x cost/performance break is demonstrated.
unknowns: Revenue share from genuinely new products.
falsifiers: If adjacencies stay immaterial to profit and core products commoditize, DI should fall.

subscores.rationale: Evidence supports structural improvement, not a 10x disruption.
Backlog, ESS deployments and UHV orders are real commercial adoption.
At least two adjacent value pools are commercial; no evidence HDHE defines an industry-wide standard.
